div.head: Rect 5.2, 5.3, 5.4, 5.5
div.ab: [5.2] Eac he sceal hwiltidum geara beon on manegum weorcum to hlafordes willan, toeacan benyrðe ⁊ bedripe ⁊ mædmæwecte. [5.3] ⁊ gyf he wel gelend bið, he sceal beon gehorsad, þæt he mæge to hlafordes seame þæt syllan oððe sylf lædan, swæðer him man tæce. [5.4] ⁊ fela ðinga swa gerad man sceal don; eal ic nu atellan ne mæig. [5.5] Ðonne him forðsið gebyrige, hede se hlaford ðæs he læfe, bute hwet friges sy.

[5.2] Et aliquotiens etiam debet esse paratus ad multas operationes uoluntatis domini sui, et ad benyrðe (id est araturam precum) et benripe (id est ad preces metere) et pratum falcare. [5.3] Et si bonam terram habeat, equum habeat, quem ad summagium domini sui prestare possit uel ipse minare, quocumque dicatur ei. [5.4] Et huiusmodi plurima facienda sunt ei, quę modo nequeunt enarrari. [5.5] Cum finis eum demediabit, habeat dominus quod relinquet, nisi forte liberum aliquid intersit.

Eac he sceal hwiltidum geara beon on ma|negum weorcum to hlafordes willan . toeacan benyrðe 7 bedripe 7 mædmæwecte . 7 gyf he wel gelend bið he sceal beon gehorsad þæt he mæge to hlafordes seame þæt syllan . oððe sylf lædan . swæðer him man tæce . 7 fela ðinga swa gerad man sceal don . eal ic nu atellan ne mæig . ðonne him forðsið gebyrige hede se hlaford ðæs he læfe bute hwet friges sy.

Eac he sceal hwiltidum geara beon on manegum weorcum to hlafordes willan, toeacan benyrðe and bedripe and mædmæwette. [5.3] And gyf he wel gelend bið, he sceal beon gehorsad þæt he mæge to hlafordes seame þæt syllan oððe sylf lædan, swæðer him man tæce. [5.4] And fela ðinga swa gerad man sceal don; eal ic nu atellan ne mæig. [5.5] Ðonne him forðsið gebyrige, hede se hlaford ðæs he læfe, bute hwet friges sy.

Auch muss er bisweilen in vielen Frohnarbeiten bereit sein, auf des Herrn Wunsch, neben Pflügen auf Geheiss [des Herrn] und Ernten auf [dessen] Forderung und Wiesenmaht. [5.3] Und wenn er gut mit Land ausgestattet ist, muss er mit einem Pferde versehen sein, damit er das zum [Tragen] herrschaftlicher Last hergeben oder selbst führen könne, welches von beiden man ihm zuweist. [5.4] Und viele Dinge muss ein so gestellter Mann leisten; alles kann ich jetzt nicht herzählen. [5.5] Wenn ihn der Tod trifft, bemächtige sich der Herr dessen, was jener hinterlässt, ausser wenn etwas von Freiem [dabei] ist.

[5.2] He must also at times be ready for many labour-services at the lord's wish, besides boon-ploughing and boon-reaping and mowing meadows [for the lord]. [5.3] And if he is well provided with land [by the lord], he must be supplied with a horse, so that he can lend it to carry the lord's loads or lead it himself, whichever [the lord] directs him. [5.4] And a man so placed must do many things; I cannot now recount them all. [5.5] When death befalls him, let the lord take what he leaves, unless something [there] is free property [stock not supplied by the lord].

Also, he must sometimes [in] the year, be [working] at many tasks, according to the lord’s will, as well as ploughing as rent, and compulsory-reaping at harvest, and mowing the meadows. And if he is well-furnished with land he must be given a horse that he may lend it to deliver the lord’s burdens or deliver them himself, whichever he is ordered, and he must do many things, all of which I may not tell now. When he dies it is fitting that the lord cares for that which he leaves [behind], except for whatever might be free.

Additionally, he must sometimes be prepared to take on many tasks at his lord’s desire, as well as required plowing, mandatory reaping, and mowing the meadows. [5.3] And if he is well provided with land, he shall be supplied with a horse that he may lend out or lead himself for the purpose of carrying his lord’s loads, whichever is commanded him. [5.4] A person thus bonded must do many things, all of which I cannot now list. [5.5] When he dies, it his appropriate that his lord should oversee whatever he leaves behind, except that which might be free of his lord’s control.
div.note: This row combines Liebermann's 5.2–5.5. The Quadripartitus read ‘benripe’ for ‘bedripe’ (same meaning). B often writes e for æ (‘hwet’ here; ‘hweges’ 14; ‘redre’ Ger 1; ‘mehte’ Ger 18). 5.2 f. is cited in 6.3. Liebermann compares 4.3c and 6.4.
This row holds several of Rabin’s sections (5.2, 5.3, 5.4, 5.5), each marked with its number.

Quadr. vermeidet erste Person 5, 1. 5, 4. 21, 4, wohl um mit dem Verf. nicht identificirt zu werden
Quadr. avoids the first person at 5, 1. 5, 4. 21, 4, probably so as not to be identified with the author
Nicht ‘ausserdem’; laut folg. Dativs ist das Wort Präposition
Not ‘besides’; as the following dative shows, the word is a preposition
Nicht ‘sein Zinsland bestellen’ (Leo); s. o. 4, 1c¹. Omnes tenentes venire debent ad III bencrthes ad arandum; Custum. Battle [o. 4, 1b²] p. 66
Not ‘till his rent-land’ (Leo); see above 4, 1c¹. Omnes tenentes venire debent ad III bencrthes ad arandum; Custum. Battle [above 4, 1b²] p. 66

Zu bedrip s. Beispiele bei Toller, auch Suppl.; New Oxford dict. s. v.; Andrews Manor 159; Vinogradoff Vill. 431; ferner Spelman Gloss. 468a. 1226. Ebenso wie ben wird bed- durch precaria, ad preces latinisiert. Es gibt Composita ned-bedrip; mete- (und Gegenteil: hunger-)bedrip (Custumal of Battle p. 164; Fines a. 1196 ed. Hunter p. 3), æle- (und Gegenteil: water-)bedrip (Hale [o. 2⁸] cxxxv; Haskins in Mél. Bémont 83; Catal. of anc. deeds II B 3708 von a. 1337), d. i. Ernte auf Geheiss mit (bzw. ohne) Speise oder Bier für die fronenden Schnitter; Lat. precaria madida (cerevisiae) im Ggs. zu sicca; Vinogradoff Vill. 174. 284; Hale lxviij. cxxiv. 66; Cust. Battle p. xxxvij; Cunningham Growth 524. Vgl. u. 21, 4³

On bedrip see the examples in Toller, also Suppl.; New Oxford dict. s. v.; Andrews Manor 159; Vinogradoff Vill. 431; further Spelman Gloss. 468a. 1226. Like ben, bed- is Latinized as precaria, ad preces. There are compounds ned-bedrip; mete- (and the opposite: hunger-)bedrip (Custumal of Battle p. 164; Fines a. 1196 ed. Hunter p. 3), æle- (and the opposite: water-)bedrip (Hale [above 2⁸] cxxxv; Haskins in Mél. Bémont 83; Catal. of anc. deeds II B 3708 of a. 1337), i.e. harvesting on demand with (or, respectively, without) food or ale for the reapers doing labour-service; Lat. precaria madida (cerevisiae) in contrast to sicca; Vinogradoff Vill. 174. 284; Hale lxviij. cxxiv. 66; Cust. Battle p. xxxvij; Cunningham Growth 524. Cf. below 21, 4³
Sweet schreibt mæweht; mæd mawan kommt oft vor; Toller s. v.
Sweet writes mæweht; mæd mawan occurs often; Toller s. v.
nicht von der Herrschaft geliefertes Stelleninventar
stock of the holding not supplied by the lordship
Wie anderer Dienst wird der des Zeidlers von der Herrschaft in Land entlohnt; vgl. Gl Bienen 3a; ein bee-furlong eines Guts in Oxfordshire kennt Williams in Archaeologia 33, 276
Like other service, that of the bee-keeper is rewarded by the lordship with land; cf. Gl Bienen 3a; Williams in Archaeologia 33, 276 knows of a bee-furlong on an estate in Oxfordshire
‘wohin’ durch Verwechselung mit hwider Q, Schmid
‘whither’ through confusion with hwider Q, Schmid
Unrichtig bezieht Q swa gerad auf þinga
Q wrongly refers swa gerad to þinga
Nicht ‘bewahre’ (Schmid), ‘nehme in Obhut’ (Leo). Richtig Q. Der Herr nimmt das Inventar zurück; s. Gl Bauer 4c. 13f.
Not ‘keep’ (Schmid), ‘take into custody’ (Leo). Q is right. The lord takes back the stock; see Gl Bauer 4c. 13f.
